line: Remember Master P told me I was the new Diddy Master P tried to sign me, but I wasn’t goin’ for it
vault_lines: Remember Master P told me I was the new Diddy
meaning:
Early in his career, Kodak was mentored by No Limit Records founder Master P. In December 2018, Kodak appeared on The Breakfast Club and claimed that Master P tried to request payment for his mentorship.

“How you gonna say, ‘Okay it ain’t about no money,’ but then turn around and be on some money shit?” Kodak asked.

Master P responded a few days later in an Instagram video. “A lot of these artists, when you try to help them, they say something crazy. The only thing I was trying to do with the little boy was help him,” he said.

line: Trademark the three and then market to moms in supermarkets

meaning: Coinciding with the release of his third mixtape, 2016’s Coloring Book, Chance released a series of monochromatic hats on his website with the number three written on them. While the concept may seem simple, his company Chance the Rapper LLC was able to trademark the style, and he even filed a lawsuit in 2017 against bootleggers of the “three hats.”

Chance references his ability to predict the future, shown earlier in the verse. He continues on to reference a famous filmmaker Orson Welles.
Welles was the creator and starred in the film Citizen Kane, a 1940’s mystery about a man’s dying words and the secrets behind his empire.

Chance intricately places this line to show the depth of his personality when he relates himself to the main character of Citizen Kane, Charles Foster Kane.

Chance also uses the line as a reference back to the Trump line, as Citizen Kane is Donald Trump’s favorite movie
